item.title: Ford takes stake in Revolution Space
item.description: Automaker to bring manufacturing expertise to Boston space company expanding from electric propulsion to complete spacecraft

item.title: Umbra unveils new family of SAR satellites
item.description: WASHINGTON — Space technology company Umbra unveiled a new line of synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellites that the company says will bring improved accuracy and an expanded capability set.

item.title: Space Beyond orders hardware for 10 more memorial cubesat missions
item.description: Space Beyond has ordered enough hardware for 10 follow-on cubesats after growing sales for the Florida startup’s first memorial spacecraft, slated to carry cremated remains into orbit in October 2027.

item.title: Upgrading cellular networks with space support
item.description: Using satellites to connect smartphones beyond the reach of cell towers is not the only way the space industry can help cellular operators plug coverage gaps.

item.title: Thruster glitch clouds BepiColombo arrival at Mercury
item.description: A joint European-Japanese mission has entered orbit around Mercury after an eight-year journey, but a premature shutdown of its thrusters has raised questions about its orbit.

item.title: With the proliferation of European satellites, we need a new approach to space-based surveillance
item.description: European space companies are expanding rapidly. They are attracting substantial investment, developing new satellite services and competing for contracts once reserved for large aerospace groups. But as more satellites enter low Earth orbit (LEO), operators face a growing problem: how can they monitor and protect the spacecraft on which communications, navigation, financial transactions and national security increasingly depend?

item.title: Space Force speeds satellite network launches
item.description: Three launches in two weeks advance SpaceX-built Space Data Network Backbone network amid concerns over procurement competition

item.title: Europe’s space community makes the case for a human spaceflight program
item.description: European government officials and companies are building the case for Europe to invest in a human spaceflight capability ahead of a key meeting next month.

item.title: China leaves 52 rocket bodies in orbit while building satellite networks
item.description: DIA official says some could remain for centuries

item.title: PiLogic testing satellite fault-prediction platform with SpaceWERX
item.description: WASHINGTON — PiLogic, a Los Angeles-based startup developing software to predict satellite failures and make spacecraft more autonomous, is working with SpaceWERX to test that capability on orbit.

item.title: Rocketdyne adapting propulsion tech for maneuverable military satellites
item.description: CEO Kristin Houston says company is exploring propulsion architectures that combine chemical thrust with electric efficiency

item.title: Turion satellites will test reconnaissance and refueling technology in GEO
item.description: Three spacecraft developed under a U.S. Space Force STRATFI contract will help the military reduce risk for its next-generation RG-XX fleet

item.title: Vyoma contracts Scanway to develop optical in-space monitoring systems for Kepler satellites
item.description: WARSAW, Poland — Scanway, an optical systems manufacturer based in Poland, has signed a contract with the German space domain awareness company Vyoma to develop optical instruments for an orbital object monitoring system. Scanway’s instruments will be incorporated into sensors that Vyoma plans to deploy on satellites operated by Canada-based Kepler Communications.

item.title: Landspace qualifies recovered Zhuque-3 engines for reuse after hot-fire tests
item.description: HELSINKI — Landspace has conducted hot-fire tests of nine engines from its recovered Zhuque-3 first stage and qualified them for reuse, marking a step toward reusability.

item.title: The Space Academy’s first test is readiness
item.description: On July 11, 1955, 306 young men were sworn in as the first class of the U.S. Air Force Academy. They did not report to the famous chapel or the campus beneath the Rampart Range, because neither existed yet. They reported to Lowry Air Force Base in Denver, a working installation with classrooms, barracks, airfields and Airmen already in place. The permanent campus in Colorado Springs did not open until 1958.

item.title: Atomic-6 tests satellite debris shielding for potential use in spacesuits
item.description: An early experiment showed promising results against debris traveling at 16,100 mph, but the technology has yet to be tested on a functioning spacesuit

item.title: Europe seeks ‘indispensable’ new roles in Artemis
item.description: Nearly eight months after NASA made major changes to Artemis, Europe is still trying to determine how it can adapt and ensure it is “indispensable” for that revised approach.

item.title: ATMOS and MBDA to explore space-based precision strike system
item.description: JOHANNESBURG — German in-space logistics startup ATMOS Space Cargo has signed a cooperation agreement with missile manufacturer MBDA Deutschland to explore the development of a capability to conduct precision strikes against ground targets from space.

item.title: GAO says Pentagon lacks a coordinated view of space supply-chain risks
item.description: The broad diagnosis is familiar: proliferated constellations are stressing manufacturing capacity, optical terminals remain a problem, and single-source suppliers create risk

item.title: New Glenn to launch Project Suncatcher data center satellites for Google
item.description: Google will launch a set of prototype data center satellites on Blue Origin’s New Glenn rocket in 2029.

item.title: Florida scientists to conduct microgravity research on Virgin Galactic flight
item.description: Two University of Florida scientists will fly on a Virgin Galactic suborbital mission to conduct microgravity experiments, continuing efforts to make such flights part of the normal research process.

item.title: RBC Signals raises $10 million for government-focused space infrastructure
item.description: Investment from Washington Harbour Partners will support expansion of government services and commercialization of emerging technologies.

item.title: Common Space picks Satellogic to build humanitarian satellite
item.description: WASHINGTON — Common Space, a non-profit building an Earth observation constellation for humanitarian use, is teaming up with Satellogic to launch its first satellite next summer.

item.title: Senate committee advances NASA and FCC nominees despite partisan dispute
item.description: The Senate Commerce Committee advanced nominees for NASA and the Federal Communications Commission despite a partisan dispute that led Democrats to boycott the session.

item.title: Sophia Space deploys on-orbit computing software
item.description: WASHINGTON — Sophia Space has deployed its first Sophia Orbital Operating System in space, a step toward establishing a baseline software layer for the company’s future on-orbit computing infrastructure.

item.title: MaiaSpace signs Space Cargo Unlimited as customer for first commercial launch
item.description: MaiaSpace, a French company developing a small launch vehicle, has signed a customer for the first commercial flight of its rocket.

item.title: Office of Space Commerce lays out 2027 priorities
item.description: GREENBELT, Md. — The director of the Office of Space Commerce said removing regulatory barriers and ensuring “American voices” are heard on the international stage are among his top priorities for the coming year.

item.title: NATO creates marketplace to buy satellite data and services
item.description: The alliance is adapting U.S. Space Force technology to its own requirements and plans to expand access to hundreds of commercial suppliers
